title: Future changes in monsoon duration and precipitation using CMIP6
problem: The understanding of future changes in monsoon duration and precipitation remains limited because regional characteristics cause significant variations and uncertainties in climate projections across different monsoon domains.
method: This study analyzes CMIP6 model outputs under three future scenarios to quantify changes in precipitation and rainy season duration for nine regional monsoons, and employs a moisture budget equation to attribute the projected precipitation changes to thermodynamic and dynamic factors.
task: The task is to project future changes in the duration and amount of summertime precipitation over various global monsoon domains using climate model simulations from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project phase 6 (CMIP6) archive.
innovation: Using CMIP6 models, this study quantifies future changes in both precipitation amount and rainy season duration across nine distinct regional monsoon domains, revealing that most monsoons will become longer and wetter primarily due to thermodynamic effects associated with global warming.
